'''"Mauler" Mithel''', designated '''DS-61-2''', was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[TIE pilot]] specially trained to be [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader's]] left wingman as a member of Vader's [[Black Squadron (Galactic Empire)/Legends|Black Squadron]]. He flew the [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE/LN starfighter]] designated [[Black 2]] during the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]].

==Biography==
{{Quote|Look out!|Mithel's last words to Darth Vader|<ref name="Episode 4">{{Film|IV}}</ref>}}
[[File:MaulerMithel-XWMG.png|thumb|left|180px|Mauler's TIE fighter during the Battle of Yavin.]]
In his youth, Mithel honed his skills poaching [[Bothan/Legends|Bothan]] [[Bothan sky dragon|sky dragons]] in his father's [[T-16 skyhopper/Legends|T-16 skyhopper]].

Mauler had a son named [[Rejlii Mithel]], who became a [[Tractor beam/Legends|tractor beam]] operator on the [[Chimaera/Legends|''Chimaera'']]. He kept a holo of Rejlii on the control yoke of his TIE fighter.

He had achieved twenty-seven Rebel kills prior to the Battle of Yavin, and he marked them by flames painted on the hull of his fighter. In addition, alongside Vader himself and fellow co-pilot "Backstabber", he had been infamously involved in various assaults on Ralltiir and Mon Calamari, which increased Black Squadron's reputation as the Empire's most feared squadron.

Mithel's fighter was with Vader's [[TIE Advanced x1/Legends|TIE Advanced x1]] when the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']] entered the battle. When Vader's right wingman was killed, Mithel panicked and tried to avoid the freighter's laser fire, only to collide with Vader's TIE Advanced. Vader was sent spinning into deep space, while Mithel was killed when his fighter impacted against the trench wall and exploded.

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Lord Vader! That energy-bolt came from above us! But, who is left to&mdash;|Mithel's final words in the Marvel Comics adaptation|<ref name="Star Wars (1977) 6">[[Star Wars (1977) 6|''Star Wars'' (1977) 6]]</ref>}}
In the [[Marvel Comics]] adaptation of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], Mithel's last words are different than seen in the film.
